judge.label: internal LLM-judge estimate (not the platform score)

missed.text: For photometric measurements of a retro-reflective device of Class IA or IB, the illuminating surface itself shall be limited to 100 cm2 though the surfaces of the retro-reflecting optical units need not necessarily attain this area.

The Class IA and IB retro-reflectors of Red colour shall have minimum RI values in mcd∙lx-1 of 3.00∙10² at angle of divergence α = 20' (Vertical β1 = 0°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), 2.00∙10² at angle of divergence α = 20' (Vertical β1 = ±10°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), 1.00∙10² at angle of divergence α = 20' (Vertical β1 = ±5°, Horizontal β2 = ±20°), 5∙10⁰ at angle of divergence α = 1°30' (Vertical β1 = 0°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), 2.8∙10⁰ at angle of divergence α = 1°30' (Vertical β1 = ±10°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), and 2.5∙10⁰ at angle of divergence α = 1°30' (Vertical β1 = ±5°, Horizontal β2 = ±20°).

When testing photometric performances of any retro-reflective device chosen at random, the conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall not be contested if no measured value deviates unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation.

The samples shall be exposed in accordance with EN ISO 4892-2:2013 using the parameters of Table A6-1: cycle 1 with a black-standard thermometer (65 ± 3 °C) or cycle 4 with a black-panel thermometer (63 ± 3 °C), exposure periods of 102 min dry and 18 min water spray, irradiance 60 ± 2 W/m² broadband (300 to 400 nm) or 0.51 ± 0.02 W/m² narrowband (340 nm), relative humidity 50 ± 10 %.

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which the lighting and light-signalling devices may be subjected, the lighting and light-signalling devices enable the vehicle to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
The lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo shall not include any logos that are not vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer logos.

Rear position lamps, rear direction-indicator lamps and rear retro-reflectors (triangular or not) may be installed on movable components only if the conditions of paragraph 5.18.1. or 5.18.2. are met.

When the vertical angle of geometric visibility below the horizontal is reduced to 5º (lamp at less than 750 mm above the ground measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the photometric field of measurements of the installed optical unit shall be permitted to be reduced to 5º below the horizontal.
Where the optional lamps are installed, the optional lamps shall be positioned at a height compatible with the requirements of the width and the symmetry of the lamps.

Where optional lamps are installed, the optional lamps shall be positioned at a vertical distance as large as the shape of the bodywork makes it possible, but not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.

Where optional rear position lamps are installed, the optional rear position lamps shall be placed at a height compatible with the applicable requirements of paragraph 6.10.4.1. and the symmetry of the lamps.

Where optional rear position lamps are installed, the optional rear position lamps shall be placed at a vertical distance as large as the shape of the bodywork makes it possible, but not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.

Where an optional lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the lamp shall have a vertical angle of 15° above and below the horizontal, except that the upward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

Where a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, for M1 and N1 category vehicles, as an alternative to paragraph 6.10.5.1., at the discretion of the manufacturer or his duly accredited representative, the rear position lamp shall have a horizontal angle of geometric visibility of 45° outwards to 45° inwards; however, where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

Where a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, for M1 and N1 category vehicles, as an alternative to paragraph 6.10.5.1., at the discretion of the manufacturer or his duly accredited representative, the rear position lamp shall have a vertical angle of geometric visibility of 15° above and below the horizontal; however, where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
When determining the unobstructed view of the apparent surface of the rear position lamp, the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light shall be excluded.
The illuminating surface of the retro-reflector shall be permitted to have parts in common with the apparent surface of any other lamp situated at the rear.
When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the limit in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m.
The ESA representative of its type shall have a measured value, expressed in dB microvolts/m, below the type approval limits.

The ESA representative of its type shall be tested for immunity to electromagnetic radiation such that test severity for the minimum test Level over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band is as given in Table 2b.

For the 24 V system starting profile (ISO 16750-2, test level II, 10 pulses), an ESA that shall be operational during engine start phases shall reach functional status class B if it performs immunity-related functions and class D if it does not, and any other ESA shall reach class C, as given in Table 3a; the starting profile applies only to ESAs that may be installed in vehicles with an internal combustion engine started by a 12 V / 24 V starter motor.

For pulse 2a, the ESA shall meet immunity test level +37 V (12V system) or +37 V (24V system) for 500 pulses with FPSC I for functions related to immunity and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity as specified in Table 3b.

For pulse 2b, the ESA shall meet immunity test level +10 V (12V system) or +20 V (24V system) for 10 pulses with FPSC II for functions related to immunity and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity as specified in Table 3b.

For pulse 3b, the ESA shall meet immunity test level +75 V (12V system) or +150 V (24V system) for 1 h with FPSC I for functions related to immunity and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity as specified in Table 3b.
In the case of front or rear position lamps, front or rear end-outline marker lamps, the arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
The arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle in the case of reversing lamps in case of reduced light distribution of two reversing lamps.

The specific identification code of the module shall comprise the starting letters “MD” for “MODULE” followed by the approval mark without the circle as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.2.1.1, in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.

Where replaceable light source module(s) is/are used and several non-identical light source modules are used, the specific identification code of the module shall be followed by additional symbols or characters.

The light source module and the lamp shall both have marks from the same applicant, where the approval mark on the light source module does not have to be the same as the one on the lamp in which the module is used, in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The lamp shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of the function(s) of that device in case an outer lens is used for several devices and bearing different approval markings.
The component shall have the markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.5.(a) affixed on it.

The position lamps or daytime running lamps, which are reciprocally incorporated with another function, using a common light source, and designed to operate permanently with an additional system to regulate the intensity of the light emitted, shall be permitted.

The logo light emitting surface (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) shall not be required to be symmetrical by itself, notwithstanding the requirements of paragraph 5.5.2. of UN Regulation No. 48, when the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside of the apparent surface of a lamp (function) incorporates only one manufacturer logo built by transparent or non-transparent components on request of the applicant.
The design of the light source module(s) shall be such that the light source module(s) can only be removed with the use of tool(s) in case of replaceable light source module(s).
The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 7 for luminous intensity and standard light distribution.
The stop lamp shall emit red light.
The measured values shall not deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the values prescribed in this Regulation.
The measured values shall correspond to the values shown in Table 12 for the minimum values required throughout the fields specified in Annexes 2 and 3.

The luminous intensity distribution shall, depending on the light source technology and in addition to paragraph 1, be checked for compliance at the point in time listed in Table A8-1, where the luminous intensity distributions at a point in time may be calculated from the luminous intensity distribution measured according to paragraph 1 by applying at each test point the ratio of luminous intensities measured at the reference coordinate of the lamp (function) under consideration.

extra.text: The ESA sample(s) of the rear lamp shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's trade name or mark and the type designation.
extra.test_case: Inspect the submitted lamp samples for a clearly legible, indelible trade name/mark and type designation; pass if both are present and survive rub testing.

extra.text: The representative ESA system(s) shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 6. and, if applicable, paragraph 7. of this Regulation for type approval to be granted.
extra.test_case: Review the test report for the representative lamp ESA; pass if all paragraph 6 requirements are met.

extra.text: The approval mark of the ESA shall comprise a circle containing the letter "E", followed by the distinguishing number of the country granting the approval.
extra.test_case: Inspect the approval mark on the lamp; pass if it shows a circle with 'E' and the approving country number.

extra.text: The approval mark of the ESA shall comprise the number of this Regulation, followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number to the right of the circle specified in paragraph 5.3.1.
extra.test_case: Inspect the approval mark on the lamp; pass if '10R-' followed by the approval number appears to the right of the E-circle.

extra.text: The electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 7.
extra.test_case: Perform broadband radiated emission measurement per Annex 7 on the lamp ESA; pass if the test is completed per the method.

extra.text: If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband limits shall be 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 6 to this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Measure broadband emissions per Annex 7 from 75 to 400 MHz; pass if all values are below the 52-63 dBµV/m limit line of Appendix 6.

extra.text: If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband limits shall be 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 7.
extra.test_case: Measure narrowband emissions per Annex 8 from 75 to 400 MHz; pass if all values are below the 42-53 dBµV/m limit line of Appendix 7.

extra.text: The maximum allowed positive pulse amplitude of transient conducted emissions generated by the ESA shall be +75 V for vehicles with 12 V systems and +150 V for vehicles with 24 V systems, as given in Table 1.
extra.test_case: Record transient emissions per ISO 7637-2; pass if positive pulse amplitudes do not exceed +75 V (12 V) or +150 V (24 V).

extra.text: For the ALSE method, the ESA shall be tested at 30 V/m in over 90 per cent and a minimum of 25 V/m over the whole of the 80 to 2,000 MHz range, and at 10 V/m in over 90 per cent and a minimum of 8 V/m over the whole of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz range (Tables 2a and 2b).
extra.test_case: Check ALSE test levels: 30/25 V/m for 80-2,000 MHz and 10/8 V/m for 2,000-6,000 MHz with no degradation.

extra.text: For the stripline method, the ESA shall be tested in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range at 60 V/m in over 90 per cent of the band (Table 2a) and a minimum of 50 V/m over the whole band (Table 2b).
extra.test_case: Check stripline test levels: 60 V/m over >90% and ≥50 V/m over 20-400 MHz with no degradation.

extra.text: For the reverberation chamber method, the ESA shall be tested at 21 V/m in over 90 per cent and a minimum of 18 V/m over the whole of the LUF to 2,000 MHz range, and at 7 V/m in over 90 per cent and a minimum of 6 V/m over the whole of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz range (Tables 2a and 2b).
extra.test_case: Check reverberation chamber levels: 21/18 V/m for LUF-2,000 MHz and 7/6 V/m for 2,000-6,000 MHz with no degradation.

extra.text: ESAs with no immunity related functions need not be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.8. and with Annex 9 to this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Assess whether lamp functions are immunity related per Annex 9; if none, radiated immunity test may be waived.

extra.text: In the frequency range 30-75 MHz, the broadband electromagnetic radiation emitted by the electrical/electronic sub-assembly (ESA) shall not exceed the reference limit E = 62 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m, measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth (see paragraphs 6.5.2.1. and 7.10.2.1.).
extra.test_case: Measure ESA broadband radiated emissions per Annex 7 from 30-75 MHz with 120 kHz bandwidth; pass if all readings are at or below 62 - 25.13 log(F/30) dBµV/m.

extra.text: In the frequency range 75-400 MHz, the broadband electromagnetic radiation emitted by the electrical/electronic sub-assembly (ESA) shall not exceed the reference limit E = 52 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m, measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth (see paragraphs 6.5.2.1. and 7.10.2.1.).
extra.test_case: Measure ESA broadband radiated emissions from 75-400 MHz with 120 kHz bandwidth; pass if all readings are at or below 52 + 15.13 log(F/75) dBµV/m.

extra.text: In the frequency range 30-75 MHz, the narrowband electromagnetic radiation emitted by the electrical/electronic sub-assembly (ESA) shall not exceed the reference limit E = 52 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m, measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth (see paragraph 6.6.2.1.).
extra.test_case: Measure ESA narrowband radiated emissions per Annex 8 from 30-75 MHz with 120 kHz bandwidth; pass if all readings are at or below 52 - 25.13 log(F/30) dBµV/m.

extra.text: If not otherwise stated in Annex 7, the measurement of broadband electromagnetic emissions from the ESA shall be performed according to CISPR 25.
extra.test_case: Review the test report to confirm that radiated broadband emissions were measured per CISPR 25 as referenced in Annex 7.

extra.text: During the radiated broadband emission test, the ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.
extra.test_case: Check the test set-up record that the lamp functions (position, stop, reversing) were energised in normal operation at maximum load during measurement.

extra.text: For ESA other than involved in "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", the radiated broadband emission test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in Clause 6.4 of CISPR 25.
extra.test_case: Verify in the test report that the ALSE method of CISPR 25 Clause 6.4 (or an OATS per CISPR 16-1-4 as alternative) was used.

extra.text: The radiated broadband emission limits apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).
extra.test_case: Verify the emission scan covers 30 to 1,000 MHz and all readings are below the applicable limits.

extra.text: If not otherwise stated in Annex 8, the narrowband electromagnetic emissions test of the ESA shall be performed according to CISPR 25.
extra.test_case: Review test report to confirm the narrowband emission test was carried out to CISPR 25 unless Annex 8 states otherwise.

extra.text: The narrowband emissions test of the ESA shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in paragraph 6.4. of CISPR 25.
extra.test_case: Confirm test setup in report follows CISPR 25 clause 6.4 ALSE arrangement (or an OATS compliant with CISPR 16-1-4 as alternative).

extra.text: The ESA may comply with the requirements of any combination of the following test methods at the manufacturer's discretion, provided that these result in the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of this Annex being covered: (a) Absorber chamber test according to ISO 11452-2; (b) TEM cell testing according to ISO 11452-3; (c) Bulk current injection testing according to ISO 11452-4; (d) Stripline testing according to ISO 11452-5; (e) Reverberation chamber test according to ISO 11452-11.
extra.test_case: Review the immunity test plan and reports to confirm that the selected ISO 11452 methods together cover the full 20 to 6,000 MHz range.

extra.text: The frequency range and general test conditions for the immunity tests of the ESA to electromagnetic radiation shall be based on ISO 11452-1.
extra.test_case: Check the test report to confirm that the frequency range and general test conditions reference ISO 11452-1.

extra.text: The test conditions for the ESA during immunity tests to electromagnetic radiation shall be according to ISO 11452-1.
extra.test_case: Audit the test report to confirm that the test conditions (temperature, supply voltage, etc.) are set per ISO 11452-1.

extra.text: The ESA under test shall be switched on and shall be stimulated to be in normal operation condition.
extra.test_case: Verify that the lamp functions (position, stop, reversing) are energised and operating normally during the immunity exposure.

extra.text: The ESA under test shall be arranged as defined in this Annex unless individual test methods dictate otherwise.
extra.test_case: Inspect the test set-up photos or drawings against the Annex 9 arrangement requirements.

extra.text: The frequency step size and dwell time shall be chosen according to ISO 11452-1.
extra.test_case: Check that the step size and dwell time in the report conform to ISO 11452-1.

extra.text: If an ESA fails the tests defined in this Annex, it shall be verified as having failed under the relevant test conditions and not as a result of the generation of uncontrolled fields.
extra.test_case: For any failure, confirm through field monitoring that the failure occurred under controlled test field conditions.

extra.text: When the absorber chamber test is used, the "substitution method" shall be used to establish the test field conditions according to ISO 11452-2.
extra.test_case: Verify that the absorber chamber report states field calibration by the substitution method per ISO 11452-2.

extra.text: When the absorber chamber test is used, the test shall be performed with vertical polarization.
extra.test_case: Confirm in the report that vertical antenna polarization was used.

extra.text: When TEM cell testing is used, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-3.
extra.test_case: Check that the TEM cell test report references and follows ISO 11452-3.

extra.text: When bulk current injection testing is used, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-4 on a test bench, either with the BCI substitution method and the injection probe positioned at 150 mm distance to the ESA, or with the BCI closed loop method and the injection probe positioned at 900 mm distance to the ESA.
extra.test_case: Verify the BCI report for an ISO 11452-4 bench set-up with the probe at 150 mm (substitution method) or 900 mm (closed loop method).

extra.text: When the reverberation chamber test is used, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-11.
extra.test_case: Check that the reverberation chamber test report follows ISO 11452-11.

extra.text: The test method shall ensure the immunity of the ESA (rear combination lamp) to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply.
extra.test_case: Perform conducted transient immunity tests per Annex 10 and confirm the lamp functions remain within the required functional status.

extra.text: The test method shall limit conducted transients from the ESA (rear combination lamp) to the vehicle power supply.
extra.test_case: Measure conducted transient emissions per Annex 10 and confirm they are within the regulation limits.

extra.text: The emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on 12/24 V supply lines shall be measured according to ISO 7637-2 on supply lines as well as on other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
extra.test_case: Measure transient conducted emissions per ISO 7637-2 on supply and operationally connected lines and compare against the regulation limits.

extra.text: In the absence of specific instructions, the height and orientation of the lamps shall be verified with the vehicle unladen and placed on a flat, horizontal surface, in the condition defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2.
extra.test_case: Measure lamp height and orientation with the unladen vehicle on a flat horizontal surface and confirm compliance.

extra.text: In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall be fitted to the vehicle symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane (based on the exterior geometrical form of the lamp and not on the edge of its illuminating surface).
extra.test_case: Measure the lateral positions of the left and right lamps relative to the median longitudinal plane; pass if symmetrical.

extra.text: In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall be symmetrical to one another in relation to the median longitudinal plane; this requirement is not valid with regard to the interior structure of the lamp.
extra.test_case: Compare the external geometry of the left and right hand lamps; pass if mirror-symmetrical about the median plane.

extra.text: In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall satisfy the same colorimetric requirements.
extra.test_case: Measure chromaticity of each function on left and right lamps; pass if both meet the same colour requirements.

extra.text: The maximum height above the ground of the lamps shall be measured from the highest point and the minimum height from the lowest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis.
extra.test_case: Measure the highest and lowest points of each function's apparent surface above ground on the vehicle and compare with height limits.

extra.text: For the purposes of reducing the geometric visibility angles, the position of a lamp with regard to height above the ground shall be measured from the H plane.
extra.test_case: Where reduced vertical visibility angles are used, measure the lamp height from the H plane and confirm the reduction condition is met.

extra.text: For the visibility of red light towards the front of a vehicle, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of a red lamp if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane situated 25 m in front of the vehicle (see Annex 4).
extra.test_case: Observe from Zone 1 at 25 m in front of the vehicle per Annex 4; no red apparent surface shall be directly visible.

extra.text: In the case of an interdependent lamp system, all light sources shall be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
extra.test_case: Switch the function and verify all light sources of the interdependent system light and extinguish simultaneously.

extra.text: The concealment of the rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and rear retro-reflectors shall be prohibited.
extra.test_case: Inspect the installation to confirm the rear lamp functions are not concealable.

extra.text: The colour of the light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
extra.test_case: Measure chromaticity of the reversing lamp and confirm it is within the white limits.

extra.text: The colour of the light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
extra.test_case: Measure chromaticity of the stop lamp and confirm it is within the red limits.

extra.text: The colour of the light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
extra.test_case: Measure chromaticity of the rear position lamp and confirm it is within the red limits.

extra.text: The colour of the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be red.
extra.test_case: Measure colour of the retro-reflected light and confirm it is red.

extra.text: The number of rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and rear retro-reflectors mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Count the installed lamps per function and compare with paragraph 6 individual specifications.

extra.text: The lamp may be installed on movable components only provided that the conditions specified in paragraphs 5.18., 5.19. and 5.20. are fulfilled.
extra.test_case: Verify compliance with paragraphs 5.18 to 5.20 for any lamp mounted on a movable component.

extra.text: Rear position lamps and rear retro-reflectors may be installed on movable components only if at all fixed positions of the movable components the lamps on the movable components meet all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for those lamps.
extra.test_case: Check position, visibility angles, colour and photometry at each fixed position of the movable component.

extra.text: The apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the rear position lamps and retro-reflectors shall not be hidden more than 50 per cent by any movable component, with or without a light-signalling device installed on it, in any fixed position different from the "normal position of use".
extra.test_case: With movable components in each fixed open position, measure the obscured portion of the apparent surface; pass if ≤ 50 %.

extra.text: With the exception of retro-reflectors, a lamp even bearing an approval mark is deemed not to be present when it cannot be made to operate by the sole installation of a light source and/or a fuse.
extra.test_case: Check on the vehicle that the rear position, stop and reversing lamps operate once light source and/or fuse are installed, without further wiring.

extra.text: If, when the lamp is installed, any part of the apparent surface of the lamp is hidden by any further parts of the vehicle, proof shall be furnished that the part of the lamp not hidden by obstacles still conforms to the photometric values prescribed for the approval of the device.
extra.test_case: Where vehicle parts hide part of the apparent surface, measure photometry of the unobstructed part and confirm it meets device approval values.

extra.text: The reversing lamp shall be present on motor vehicles (mandatory).
extra.test_case: Inspect the M1 vehicle installation and confirm at least one reversing lamp is fitted.

extra.text: On motor vehicles of category M1, one reversing lamp device is mandatory and a second device is optional.
extra.test_case: Count the reversing lamps installed on the M1 vehicle; pass if one or two are fitted.

extra.text: For reversing lamp devices installed at the rear of the vehicle, the geometric visibility defined by angle α as specified in paragraph 2.10.7. shall be α = 15° upwards and 5° downwards.
extra.test_case: Verify on the vehicle that the apparent surface is visible over 15° upwards and 5° downwards.

extra.text: For reversing lamp devices installed at the rear of the vehicle, if there is only one device, the geometric visibility defined by angle β as specified in paragraph 2.10.7. shall be β = 45° to right and to left.
extra.test_case: Verify visibility of the apparent surface over 45° to the right and left of the single device.

extra.text: The reversing lamp shall be oriented rearwards.
extra.test_case: Inspect the installation and confirm the reference axis of the reversing lamp points rearwards.

extra.text: For the reversing lamp, a tell-tale indicating failure is mandatory if required by the component regulation.
extra.test_case: Check the component approval; if failure indication is required, simulate failure and confirm the tell-tale activates.

extra.text: Stop lamp devices of S1 or S2 categories shall be mandatory on all categories of vehicles (including M1).
extra.test_case: Inspect the M1 vehicle installation and confirm that S1 or S2 category stop lamp devices are fitted.

extra.text: In length, S1 or S2 categories stop lamps shall be positioned at the rear of the vehicle.
extra.test_case: Inspect the vehicle installation; pass if the stop lamps are located at the rear of the vehicle.

extra.text: For stop lamps of categories S1 and S2 mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward horizontal angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
extra.test_case: Measure mounting height; if below 750 mm verify inward visibility of at least 20° under the H plane.

extra.text: Where an S1 or S2 category stop lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward vertical angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
extra.test_case: Measure mounting height; if below 750 mm verify downward visibility of at least 5°.

extra.text: The S1 or S2 category stop lamps shall be oriented towards the rear of the vehicle.
extra.test_case: Inspect installation; pass if the stop lamp reference axis points rearwards.

extra.text: Rear position lamps of R or R1 or R2 categories shall be mandatory.
extra.test_case: Inspect the vehicle; pass if rear position lamps of category R, R1 or R2 are fitted.

extra.text: Where a rear position lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward horizontal angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
extra.test_case: Measure mounting height; if below 750 mm verify inward visibility of at least 20° under the H plane.

extra.text: The rear position lamps shall be oriented rearwards.
extra.test_case: Inspect installation; pass if the rear position lamp reference axis points rearwards.

extra.text: In all cases, the distance between the rear fog-lamp and each stop-lamp shall be greater than 100 mm.
extra.test_case: Measure on the vehicle the distance between the rear fog lamp and each stop lamp of the rear lamp; pass if greater than 100 mm.

extra.text: The rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, is mandatory on motor vehicles.
extra.test_case: Verify that the M1 vehicle is fitted with non-triangular rear retro-reflectors.

extra.text: In height, the rear retro-reflector shall be above the ground not less than 250 mm nor more than 900 mm (not more than 1,200 mm if grouped with any rear lamp(s), 1,500 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900 mm or 1,200 mm respectively).
extra.test_case: Measure the height of the retro-reflector above ground per paragraph 5.8.1.; pass if between 250 mm and 900 mm (1,200 mm if grouped with rear lamps, 1,500 mm where bodywork prevents).

extra.text: In length, the rear retro-reflector shall be at the rear of the vehicle.
extra.test_case: Inspect the vehicle and verify the retro-reflector is located at the rear.

extra.text: The orientation of the rear retro-reflector shall be rearwards.
extra.test_case: Inspect the installation and verify the retro-reflector reference axis faces rearwards.

extra.text: When daytime running lamps are switched ON, the rear position lamps shall be switched ON.
extra.test_case: On the vehicle, activate the daytime running lamps and verify by inspection that the rear position lamps of the rear lamp are switched ON.

extra.text: Where the emergency stop signal is provided by the stop lamps, the emergency stop signal shall be given by the simultaneous operation of all the stop lamps fitted as described in paragraph 6.23.7.
extra.test_case: Trigger the emergency stop signal on the vehicle and check that all fitted stop lamps operate simultaneously.

extra.text: All the lamps of the emergency stop signal shall flash in phase at a frequency of 4.0 ± 1.0 Hz.
extra.test_case: Activate the emergency stop signal and measure the flash frequency and phase of all stop lamps; pass if they are in phase at 3.0-5.0 Hz.

extra.text: The emergency stop signal shall operate independently of other lamps.
extra.test_case: Activate the emergency stop signal with the other lamps in various states and check that its operation is unaffected.

extra.text: The emergency stop signal shall be switched ON and OFF automatically.
extra.test_case: Check that no manual control exists and that the signal is switched ON and OFF automatically.

extra.text: The emergency stop signal shall be switched ON only when the vehicle speed is above 50 km/h and the braking system is providing the emergency braking logic signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H.
extra.test_case: Perform braking tests above and below 50 km/h, with and without the emergency braking logic signal; pass if activation occurs only above 50 km/h with the signal present.

extra.text: The emergency stop signal shall be automatically switched OFF if the emergency braking logic signal as defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H is no longer provided or if the hazard warning signal is activated.
extra.test_case: Remove the emergency braking logic signal, or activate the hazard warning signal, and check that the emergency stop signal switches OFF automatically.

extra.text: For the verification of the visibility of a red lamp to the front (paragraph 5.10.4.), the zone 1 explored by the eye of the observer shall be bounded in height by two horizontal planes 1 m and 2.2 m respectively above the ground.
extra.test_case: Check on the vehicle that no red light from the rear position or stop lamp is directly visible from the front within the zone between 1 m and 2.2 m above ground.

extra.text: For the verification of the visibility of a red lamp to the front (paragraph 5.10.4.), the zone 1 explored by the eye of the observer shall be bounded in width by a vertical plane which, forming to the front an angle of 15° outwards from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane, passes through the point or points of contact of vertical planes parallel to the vehicle's median longitudinal plane delimiting the vehicle's overall width.
extra.test_case: Observe from the front zone bounded by the 15° outward planes through the vehicle width contact points and verify no red light from the rear lamp is directly visible.

extra.text: When two or more lamps are part of the same unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, approval may be granted only if each of these lamps (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp, retro-reflector) satisfy the provisions set out in this Regulation or in another Regulation.
extra.test_case: Check that each function in the combination lamp holds or meets the requirements of its applicable Regulation (R148, R150).

extra.text: Lamps not satisfying the provisions of any of those Regulations shall not be part of the unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps.
extra.test_case: Review the function list of the unit and confirm that no non-compliant or unapproved function is integrated.

extra.text: The rear position lamp shall be identified by the symbol R1 (steady) or R2 (variable).
extra.test_case: Check that the marking shows R1 or R2, matching the intensity control of the rear position lamp.

extra.text: The reversing lamp shall be identified by the symbol AR (the letters A and R may be mingled).
extra.test_case: Check that the marking shows the symbol AR.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
extra.test_case: Inspect the marking for a circled E followed by the country number.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the four to six-digit sequential number, being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
extra.test_case: Inspect the marking for a 4 to 6 digit sequential number matching the approval number.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the symbols identifying the light signalling lamps prescribed in paragraph 3.2.4.
extra.test_case: Inspect the marking for the function symbols per Table 1.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the number of this Regulation followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
extra.test_case: Inspect the marking for "148R" followed by the series digits (e.g. 01).

extra.text: In the case of rear position lamps, the horizontal arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
extra.test_case: With the lamp in its mounting position, check that the arrow points outboard.

extra.text: Lamps, with the exception of lamps with non-replaceable light sources, shall bear a marking indicating the category or categories of light source(s) prescribed.
extra.test_case: If the light sources are replaceable, inspect for the light source category marking.

extra.text: Lamps with an electronic light source control gear shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage.
extra.test_case: Inspect for a rated voltage or voltage range marking.

extra.text: Lamps with a variable luminous intensity control shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage.
extra.test_case: Inspect for a rated voltage or voltage range marking.

extra.text: An electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control being part of the lamp, but not included into the lamp body, shall be marked with its identification number and the name of the manufacturer.
extra.test_case: Inspect the external control gear for an identification number and the manufacturer name.

extra.text: Where a single approval mark is affixed to the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, the approval marking shall be visible after their installation.
extra.test_case: Inspect the lamp installed on a representative vehicle mounting and confirm the single approval mark is visible.

extra.text: Where a single approval mark is affixed to the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, no part of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps that transmits light can be removed without at the same time removing the approval mark.
extra.test_case: Review the design/drawing and check that every light-transmitting part (e.g. outer lens) carries or is inseparable from the approval mark.

extra.text: Each lamp submitted for approval shall conform to the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5.
extra.test_case: Verify by test report that the rear position, stop and reversing lamps meet all requirements of paragraphs 4 and 5.

extra.text: The requirements contained in sections 5 "General specifications" and 6 "Individual specifications" (and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections) of UN Regulation No. 48 and its series of amendments in force at the time of application for the lamp type approval shall apply, the requirements pertinent to each lamp and to the M1 vehicle category being applied where their verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.
extra.test_case: Check the lamp against the R48 sections 5 and 6 provisions for rear position, stop and reversing lamps on M1 vehicles that are verifiable at lamp approval (e.g. geometric visibility, apparent surface).

extra.text: In a single lamp containing more than one light source, a group of light sources, wired so that the failure of any one of them causes all of them to stop emitting light, shall be considered to be one light source.
extra.test_case: Review the LED wiring diagram of each function to identify the light-source groups considered as one light source for failure assessment.

extra.text: In case of failure of any one light source in a single reversing lamp containing more than one light source, the light intensity shall comply with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3 and when all light sources are illuminated the maximum intensities shall not be exceeded, or a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure shall be produced.
extra.test_case: Simulate single light-source failure in the reversing lamp and check intensities remain above Annex 3 minima, or a failure signal is produced.

extra.text: In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a rear position lamp category R2 emitting more than the maximum value of category R1, requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.
extra.test_case: Simulate failure of the variable intensity control and verify the lamp automatically reverts to steady intensity within R1 limits.

extra.text: In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the design of the lamp shall be such that the light source(s) can be fixed in no other position but the correct one.
extra.test_case: Attempt to insert the light source in incorrect orientations and confirm only the correct position is possible.

extra.text: In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the light source(s) holder shall conform to the characteristics given in IEC Publication 60061, applying the holder data sheet relevant to the category of light source(s) prescribed and, where a category of LED substitute light source(s) is also prescribed, the holder data sheet relevant to that category.
extra.test_case: Gauge the holder against the relevant IEC 60061 data sheet(s).

extra.text: All photometric and colorimetric measurements shall be made with respect to the conditions of paragraph 4.8., with the particulars of the methods of measurement given in Annex 3.
extra.test_case: Review test report to confirm photometric and colorimetric measurements followed paragraph 4.8 conditions and Annex 3 methods.

extra.text: During photometric measurements, stray reflections shall be avoided by appropriate masking.
extra.test_case: Inspect the photometric set-up and confirm that masking is in place to prevent stray reflections.

extra.text: If not otherwise specified, the intensities shall be measured with the light source continuously lit.
extra.test_case: Verify that the rear position, stop and reversing lamps were measured with steady (continuous) operation.

extra.text: The limits of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of each light-signalling lamp shall be determined.
extra.test_case: Confirm that the apparent surface limits along the reference axis are documented for the position, stop and reversing lamps.

extra.text: For a lamp controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, the lamp shall be operated as specified by the applicant.
extra.test_case: Confirm that the test operating conditions match the applicant's declared control gear settings.

extra.text: For a lamp not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control and with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), the lamp shall be operated as specified by the applicant.
extra.test_case: Confirm that the lamp was operated under the applicant-declared conditions during the test.

extra.text: If a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp producing either steady or variable luminous intensity, the ratio between the luminous intensities measured of the two lamps turned on simultaneously and the intensity of the rear position lamp turned on alone should be at least 5:1 in the field delimited by ±5° V and ±10° H of the light distribution table.
extra.test_case: Measure the combined stop+position intensity against the position-only intensity at grid points within ±5° V / ±10° H and confirm a ratio of at least 5:1.

extra.text: Tests for compliance of the luminous intensities shall be carried out according to Annex 8.
extra.test_case: Confirm that the photometric test procedure follows Annex 8.

extra.text: To check the colorimetric characteristics, the test procedure described in paragraph 4.8. shall be applied.
extra.test_case: Verify that the colorimetric test conditions (voltage, operation) match paragraph 4.8.

extra.text: For lamps equipped with non-replaceable light sources, the colorimetric characteristics should be verified with the light sources present in the lamp, in accordance with relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 4.8.
extra.test_case: Confirm that the colour measurement was done with the LEDs fitted in the lamp.

extra.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of rear position lamp supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 4.
extra.test_case: Measure both rear position lamp samples and compare them with Table 4.

extra.text: For rear position lamps of category R1 (steady), the minimum luminous intensity shall be 4 cd and the maximum luminous intensity shall be 17 cd when used as a single lamp, with the standard light distribution per Figure A3-I.
extra.test_case: Measure HV ≥ 4 cd, max ≤ 17 cd, and the Figure A3-I grid values.

extra.text: For rear position lamps of category R2 (variable), the minimum luminous intensity shall be 4 cd and the maximum luminous intensity shall be 42 cd when used as a single lamp (21 cd for a lamp marked "D"), with the standard light distribution per Figure A3-I.
extra.test_case: Measure HV ≥ 4 cd and max ≤ 42 cd (≤ 21 cd if marked D) across the variable intensity range.

extra.text: Within the angles of geometric visibility defined in Table A2-1, the rear position lamp shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 0.05 cd as specified in Table 4.
extra.test_case: Measure across the Table A2-1 angles and confirm ≥ 0.05 cd.

extra.text: For a stop lamp of category S1 (steady), the minimum luminous intensity shall be 6.0∙10^1 cd, the maximum luminous intensity shall be 2.60∙10^2 cd when used as a single lamp or 1.30∙10^2 cd when used as a lamp marked "D", the standard light distribution shall be as defined in Figure A3-I, and within the angles of geometric visibility defined in Table A2-1 the minimum luminous intensity shall be 3∙10^-1 cd, as given in Table 7.
extra.test_case: Measure intensity on reference axis, at Figure A3-I grid points and across Table A2-1 angles; values within 60-260 cd (130 cd if 'D') and ≥0.3 cd in geometric visibility field.

extra.text: For a stop lamp of category S2 (variable), the minimum luminous intensity shall be 6.0∙10^1 cd, the maximum luminous intensity shall be 7.30∙10^2 cd when used as a single lamp or 3.65∙10^2 cd when used as a lamp marked "D", the standard light distribution shall be as defined in Figure A3-I, and within the angles of geometric visibility defined in Table A2-1 the minimum luminous intensity shall be 3∙10^-1 cd (day) and 7∙10^-2 cd (night), as given in Table 7.
extra.test_case: Measure in day and night modes; intensities within 60-730 cd (365 cd if 'D') and ≥0.3 cd day / 0.07 cd night within Table A2-1 angles.

extra.text: The minimum luminous intensity of the stop lamp within the angles of geometric visibility shall be as specified in Table 7.
extra.test_case: Measure intensity across the Table A2-1 angular field; values not below the Table 7 minimum for the category.

extra.text: The stop lamp shall comply with the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
extra.test_case: Simulate light source failure per paragraph 4.6 and verify the specified behaviour.

extra.text: For a reversing lamp of category AR, the minimum luminous intensity shall be 8.0∙10^1 cd, as given in Table 10.
extra.test_case: Measure intensity on the reference axis; value ≥80 cd.

extra.text: For a reversing lamp of category AR, the maximum luminous intensity in or above the H-plane shall be 3.00∙10^2 cd, as given in Table 10.
extra.test_case: Scan intensity in and above the H-plane; no value exceeds 300 cd.

extra.text: For a reversing lamp of category AR, the maximum luminous intensity below the H-plane, down to 5°D, shall be 6.00∙10^2 cd, as given in Table 10.
extra.test_case: Scan intensity between H-plane and 5°D; no value exceeds 600 cd.

extra.text: For a reversing lamp of category AR, the standard light distribution shall be as defined in Figure A3-V, as given in Table 10.
extra.test_case: Measure at Figure A3-V grid points; values meet the required percentages of the minimum.

extra.text: The rear position lamp (R1, R2) shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard / 80° outboard, as given in Table A2-1 (angles shown are for lamps mounted on the right side of the vehicle).
extra.test_case: Goniometric check of the rear position lamp confirms visibility of the apparent surface over at least 45° inboard and 80° outboard.

extra.text: The rear position lamp (R1, R2) shall have minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above / 15° below the H-plane, as given in Table A2-1.
extra.test_case: Goniometric check confirms rear position lamp visibility at least 15° above and 15° below the H-plane.

extra.text: For a rear position lamp (R1, R2) mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm, the reduced minimum horizontal angles of 20° inboard / 80° outboard may be used only below the H-plane.
extra.test_case: Check that below the H-plane the rear position lamp is visible at least 20° inboard and 80° outboard, and full 45°/80° above the H-plane.

extra.text: For a rear position lamp (R1, R2) to be installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm, the minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility shall be 15° above / 5° below.
extra.test_case: Goniometric check confirms rear position lamp visibility at least 15° above and 5° below the H-plane.

extra.text: Unless specified otherwise, the values shown in Figures A3-I to A3-XV give, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities as a percentage of the minimum intensities required, which shall be mathematically rounded down to three significant digits.
extra.test_case: Compute the required minimum at each grid point as the percentage of the required minimum, rounded down to three significant digits, and verify measured intensities meet it.

extra.text: Where the rear position lamps are intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity is verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
extra.test_case: If the declared mounting height is ≤ 750 mm, verify rear position lamp photometry down to 5° below horizontal only and confirm compliance there.

extra.text: Where the stop lamps of category S1, S2 or MS are intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity is verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
extra.test_case: If the declared mounting height is ≤ 750 mm, verify S1/S2 stop lamp photometry down to 5° below horizontal only and confirm compliance there.

extra.text: The rear position lamps shall meet, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities as a percentage of the minimum intensities required (see Tables 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8) given by the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement of the rear position lamp at the Figure A3-I points; each value shall be at least the stated percentage of the required minimum.

extra.text: The stop lamps of category S1, S2 or MS shall meet, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities as a percentage of the minimum intensities required (see Table 7) given by the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement of the stop lamp at the Figure A3-I points; each value shall be at least the stated percentage of the Table 7 minimum.

extra.text: The reversing lamps shall meet, at the measuring points expressed in degrees of angle with the axis of reference, the minimum intensities in cd of the light emitted given in Figure A3-V.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement of the reversing lamp at the Figure A3-V points; each value shall be at least the stated cd value.

extra.text: Depending on the light source technology, the luminous intensity distribution of the rear position lamp is, in addition to paragraph 1, checked for compliance at 4 seconds after switch ON, with HV as the reference coordinate, as listed in Table A8-1.
extra.test_case: Check the rear position lamp intensity distribution at 4 s after switch ON (scaled by the HV ratio); it must meet the min/max limits.

extra.text: In case a lamp (function) uses LED technology only, the lamp (function) is deemed to comply with the corresponding intensity requirements at all points in time, if the values measured according to paragraph 1.2. are compliant.
extra.test_case: Confirm that each function uses LEDs only and that the paragraph 1.2 measurements comply; compliance at all points in time is then deemed.

extra.text: A separate approval is required for the retro-reflector (Class IA or IB) as a retro-reflective device listed in paragraph 1.
extra.test_case: Check that a separate UN R150 approval exists for the retro-reflector of the rear lamp.

extra.text: The approval number assigned to the approved type of retro-reflector shall be marked on the device following the requirements of paragraph 3.3.
extra.test_case: Inspect the retro-reflector sample for the approval number marked per paragraph 3.3.

extra.text: The symbol identifying the retro-reflector shall be "IA" for a retro-reflector for motor vehicles (independent) or "IB" for a retro-reflector for motor vehicles combined with other signal lamps which are not watertight, with a minimum "a" of 5 mm, as given in Table 1.
extra.test_case: Verify the class symbol on the marking matches the class of the retro-reflector (IA or IB) and the lamp watertightness.

extra.text: With regard to the size of the approval marking, the value for "a" shall be as defined in Table 1 (minimum 5 mm for Class IA and IB retro-reflectors).
extra.test_case: Measure the approval mark dimension "a" and confirm it is at least 5 mm.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
extra.test_case: Inspect the marking for a circle surrounding "E" and the country distinguishing number.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the symbols identifying the retro-reflective device prescribed in paragraph 3.2.5.
extra.test_case: Inspect the marking for the class symbol IA or IB per Table 1.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the number of this Regulation followed by the letter "R" and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
extra.test_case: Inspect the marking for "150R" followed by the two-digit series of amendments.

extra.text: In case of a retro-reflector of Class IA or IB, the retro-reflector shall bear the word "TOP" inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface, if such an indication is necessary to determine without ambiguity the angle or angles of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer.
extra.test_case: Check whether the retro-reflector is rotation-sensitive and, if so, that "TOP" is inscribed horizontally at the highest part of the illuminating surface.

extra.text: Where a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or Unique Identifier is affixed to the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, this marking shall be visible after their installation.
extra.test_case: With the lamp installed on the vehicle, verify the single approval mark is visible.

extra.text: Where a single approval mark is affixed to the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, no part of the lamps that transmits light can be removed without at the same time removing the approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or the Unique Identifier.
extra.test_case: Inspect construction to confirm that no light-transmitting part can be removed without removing the single approval mark.

extra.text: The requirements contained in sections 5. "General specifications" and 6. "Individual specifications" and in the Annexes referenced in those sections of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86, and their series of amendments in force at the time of application for the retro-reflecting device type approval, shall apply to the retro-reflector; the requirements pertinent to the retro-reflector and to the vehicle category (M1) on which it is intended to be installed shall be applied where their verification at the moment of type approval is feasible.
extra.test_case: Review the retro-reflector against the applicable R48 sections 5 and 6 provisions verifiable at type approval; all feasible checks must pass.

extra.text: After verification of the general specifications (paragraph 4.) and the specifications of shape and dimensions (Annex 5), the ten samples of the retro-reflector shall be subjected to the heat resistance test described in Part 1 of Annex 6 and at least one hour after this test examined as to their colorimetric characteristics in paragraph 5.1.5. and RI in paragraph 5.1.4., for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° or if necessary in the position defined in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.
extra.test_case: Perform the Annex 6 Part 1 heat test on ten samples, then after ≥1 h measure colour and RI at 20', 0°/0°; values must comply.

extra.text: The two retro-reflectors giving the minimum and maximum values after the heat resistance test shall be fully tested as shown in paragraph 5.1.4.
extra.test_case: Fully measure RI at all Table 3 angles on the min and max samples; all values must meet paragraph 5.1.4.

extra.text: The first group of two retro-reflector samples shall be subjected successively to the water penetration test (Part 2 of Annex 6) and then, if this test is satisfactory, to the tests for resistance to fuels and lubricants (Parts 1 and 2 of Annex 7).
extra.test_case: Perform the water penetration test followed by the fuel and lubricant resistance tests; samples must pass.

extra.text: The second group of two retro-reflector samples shall, if necessary, be subjected to the corrosion test in Part 4 of Annex 6, and then to the abrasive-strength test of the rear face of the retro-reflective device in Part 5 of Annex 6.
extra.test_case: Perform the corrosion test (if applicable) and the rear-face abrasion test; samples must pass.

extra.text: The third group of two retro-reflector samples shall be subjected to the test for stability in time of the optical properties of retro-reflective device in Part 3 of Annex 4.
extra.test_case: Perform the Annex 4 Part 3 stability test; samples must retain compliant optical properties.

extra.text: The fourth group of two retro-reflector samples shall be subjected to the resistance to weathering test (Part 6 of Annex 6).
extra.test_case: Perform the Annex 6 Part 6 weathering test; samples must pass.

extra.text: After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each group shall have a colour which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.5.
extra.test_case: Measure colour after each test group; chromaticity must satisfy paragraph 5.1.5.

extra.text: For a red retro-reflector of Class IA or IB, at an angle of divergence of 20', the RI shall be at least 300 mcd/lx at β1 = 0°, β2 = 0°; 200 mcd/lx at β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°; and 100 mcd/lx at β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°.
extra.test_case: Measure RI at 20' divergence at the three illumination angle sets; values must be ≥300, ≥200 and ≥100 mcd/lx respectively.

extra.text: Where the retro-reflector of Class IA or Class IB is intended to be installed with its H plane at a mounting height less than 750 mm above the ground, the RI values shall be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
extra.test_case: Confirm mounting height; if <750 mm, verify RI downward angles only to 5° and check compliance.

extra.text: The testing of the colour of the retro-reflector (night-time colour) shall be carried out according to the method described in paragraph 4.2.1.
extra.test_case: Verify the colour test report uses the paragraph 4.2.1 method (Illuminant A, 1/3°, 0°/0°).

extra.text: The retro-reflectors of Classes IA and IB shall be subjected to the tests in the chronological order given in Table 4 (Chronological order of tests, Classes IA, IB, IIIA and IIIB).
extra.test_case: Review the test report and confirm the samples were tested in the Table 4 sequence.

extra.text: For retro-reflectors of Classes IA and IB, the samples shall be subjected to the heat test of Part 1 of Annex 6 (48 h at 65 °C ± 2 °C), followed by a visual inspection for distortion.
extra.test_case: Expose the samples for 48 h at 65 ± 2 °C, then inspect them; no distortion shall be visible.

extra.text: When the RI of the retro-reflective device is measured for an angle β of β1 = β2 = 0°, it shall be ascertained whether any mirror effect is produced by slightly turning the device.
extra.test_case: During goniophotometric measurement at β1 = β2 = 0°, turn the retro-reflector slightly and check for a mirror effect.

extra.text: If any mirror effect is produced, a reading of the RI of the retro-reflective device shall be taken with an angle β of β1 = -5°, β2 = 0°.
extra.test_case: If a mirror effect is observed, measure RI at β1 = -5°, β2 = 0° and use that reading.

extra.text: For retro-reflective devices not marked "TOP", when the RI is measured for the other angles of illumination and divergence, the retro-reflective device shall be placed in the position corresponding to this value of ε (minimum RI), and if the specified values are not attained, the device may be rotated about its axis of reference only within ±5° from that position.
extra.test_case: Measure RI at all other illumination/divergence angles at the minimum-RI ε position (±5° allowed) and verify specified values are met.

extra.text: With an illumination angle β of β1 = β2 = 0°, or the angle specified in paragraph 4. of this Regulation, and an angle of divergence of 20', retro-reflective devices marked "TOP" shall be rotated about their axes ±5°.
extra.test_case: Rotate the TOP-marked retro-reflector ±5° about its axis at β = 0°, α = 20' while measuring RI.

extra.text: If for the direction β1 = β2 = 0°, and for ε = 0° the RI exceeds the specified value by 50 per cent or more, all measurements for all angles of illumination and divergence shall be made for ε = 0°.
extra.test_case: If RI at β = 0°, ε = 0° is ≥150 % of the specified value, perform all measurements at ε = 0° and verify compliance.

extra.text: For testing the retro-reflection the retro-reflective devices shall be illuminated with a CIE Standard Illuminant A (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) and measured as described in Part 1 of Annex 4.
extra.test_case: Verify the test source is CIE Standard Illuminant A and the procedure follows Annex 4 Part 1.

extra.text: For moulded plastics reflectors of retro-reflecting devices of Classes IA and IB, the retro-reflective device shall be kept for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at a temperature of 65 °C ± 2 °C, after which the sample shall be allowed to cool for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C.
extra.test_case: Condition the retro-reflector 48 h at 65 °C ± 2 °C dry, then cool 1 h at 23 °C ± 2 °C, and record the conditioning log.

extra.text: For the water penetration test, the retro-reflective device, whether part of a lamp or not, shall be stripped of all removable parts and immersed for 10 minutes in water at a temperature of 50 °C ± 5 °C, the highest point of the upper part of the illuminating surface being 20 mm below the surface of the water.
extra.test_case: Strip removable parts and immerse the device 10 min in water at 50 °C ± 5 °C with the top of the illuminating surface 20 mm below the water surface.

extra.text: The water immersion test shall be repeated after turning the retro-reflective device through 180°, so that the illuminating surface is at the bottom and the rear face is covered by about 20 mm of water.
extra.test_case: Repeat the 50 °C immersion with the device inverted, rear face under about 20 mm of water.

extra.text: The retro-reflective device sample units shall then be immediately immersed in the same conditions in water at a temperature of 25 °C ± 5 °C.
extra.test_case: Immediately after the 50 °C immersions, immerse the device under the same conditions in water at 25 °C ± 5 °C.

extra.text: If visual inspection does not reveal the presence of water or in case of doubt, the RI of the retro-reflector shall be measured by the method described in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation, the retro-reflective device being first lightly shaken to remove excess water from the outside.
extra.test_case: After lightly shaking off external water, measure the RI per paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. and check compliance with the required values.

extra.text: As an alternative, at the request of the manufacturer, the moisture and dust tests of Annex 6 Part 3 shall be applied to the Class IB retro-reflective device.
extra.test_case: Check the test report shows the moisture and dust tests of Annex 6 Part 3 were applied when the manufacturer chose this alternative.

extra.text: Since the retro-reflector is reciprocally incorporated or grouped with signalling or lighting functions, these functions shall be operated at design voltage during the water spray test according to a cycle of 5 min ON (in flashing mode, where appropriate), 55 min OFF.
extra.test_case: Check the test log shows the rear position, stop and reversing functions were cycled 5 min ON / 55 min OFF at design voltage.

extra.text: Upon completion of the drain period, no standing pool of water shall be allowed to be formed in the device, or which can be formed by tapping or tilting the device.
extra.test_case: Inspect the interior, then tap and tilt the device; pass if no standing pool of water is present or forms.

extra.text: Upon completion of the drain period, the RI shall be measured according to the method specified in Part 1 of Annex 4 after having dried the exterior of the device with a dry cotton cloth.
extra.test_case: Dry the exterior with a dry cotton cloth and measure the RI per Annex 4 Part 1; compare it with the initial RI.

extra.text: Upon completion of the dust exposure test, the exterior of the device shall be cleaned and dried with a dry cotton cloth and the RI measured according to the method specified in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Clean and dry the exterior, measure the RI per paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. and evaluate it against the initial RI.

extra.text: The retro-reflective device, or the lamp if the device is combined with a light, shall be stripped of all removable parts and subjected to the action of a saline mist for a period of 50 hours, comprising two periods of exposure of 24 hours each, separated by an interval of two hours during which the sample is allowed to dry.
extra.test_case: Check the test record shows the combination lamp, stripped of removable parts, was exposed to 2 x 24 h saline mist with a 2 h drying interval.

extra.text: After the corrosion test, the coefficient of retro-reflection RA of the retro-reflective areas, when measured after a recovery period of 48 hours as specified in Part 2 of Annex 6, at an entrance angle of β2 = 5° and an observation angle of α = 20', shall be not less than the value in Table 9 or more than the value in Table 10 respectively.
extra.test_case: After 48 h recovery, measure RA at β2 = 5°, α = 20' and compare against Table 9 minimum and Table 10 maximum.

extra.text: For moulded plastics reflectors of Classes IA and IB with an accessible mirror-backed rear face, the reverse side of the retro-reflective device shall be brushed with a hard nylon brush.
extra.test_case: Verify the test record shows the rear face was brushed with a hard nylon brush.

extra.text: After having brushed the rear face, in the case of moulded plastics reflectors of Classes IA and IB, a cotton cloth soaked in the mixture defined in Part 1 of Annex 7 shall be applied to the said rear face for one minute, after which the cloth is removed and the retro-reflective device left to dry.
extra.test_case: Apply a cotton cloth soaked in the Annex 7 Part 1 mixture to the rear face for 1 min, remove and let dry.

extra.text: For mirror-backed retro-reflective devices with accessible rear face, the RI shall then be measured, according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation, after the whole surface of the mirror-backed rear face has been covered with Indian ink.
extra.test_case: Cover the rear face with Indian ink, measure RI per paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. and check compliance with the required values.

extra.text: In case of retro-reflective devices, the samples shall be exposed to accelerated artificial weathering in accordance with EN ISO 4892-2:2013 for a period of 500 hours.
extra.test_case: Verify from the test log that the retro-reflector samples were exposed for 500 hours.

extra.text: For the resistance to fuels test, a test mixture of 70 vol. per cent of n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent of toluol shall be applied to the retro-reflective device.
extra.test_case: Confirm the fuel resistance test used a 70/30 vol.% n-heptane/toluol mixture on the retro-reflector.

extra.text: After about five minutes following the wiping with the test mixture, the surface of the retro-reflective device shall be inspected visually and must not show any apparent surface changes, except that slight surface cracks will not be objected to.
extra.test_case: Visually inspect the surface about five minutes after wiping; pass if no apparent surface change other than slight surface cracks.

extra.text: The outer surface of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, of the illuminating surface, shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in the test mixture of 70 vol. per cent n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent toluol.
extra.test_case: Wipe the retro-reflector outer/illuminating surface with a cotton cloth soaked in the test mixture and record the procedure.

extra.text: For moulded plastics reflectors of Classes IA and IB, after the lubricating oil exposure and cleaning, the RI of the retro-reflective device shall be measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Measure RI per paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. after the oil test and verify the values meet the limits required by that paragraph.

extra.text: For moulded plastics reflectors of Classes IA and IB, the outer surface of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, the illuminating surface, shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a detergent lubricating oil.
extra.test_case: Wipe the outer and illuminating surface with a cotton cloth soaked in detergent lubricating oil and record that the exposure was applied.

extra.text: For moulded plastics reflectors of Classes IA and IB, after about 5 minutes of exposure to the detergent lubricating oil, the surface of the retro-reflective device shall be cleaned.
extra.test_case: After about 5 minutes of oil exposure, clean the surface and confirm it is free of residue before measurement.

extra.text: In the approval mark affixed to the retro-reflective device, the approval number must be placed close to, but in any position in relation to, the circle surrounding the letter "E".
extra.test_case: Inspect the approval mark on the retro-reflector and confirm the approval number is located close to the circle surrounding the letter E.

extra.text: In the approval mark affixed to the retro-reflective device, the digits constituting the approval number must face the same way as the "E".
extra.test_case: Inspect the approval mark and confirm the approval number digits are oriented in the same direction as the letter E.

extra.text: In the approval mark affixed to the retro-reflective device, the group of symbols indicating the class must be diametrically opposite the approval number.
extra.test_case: Inspect the approval mark and confirm the class symbol (e.g. IA or IB) is placed diametrically opposite the approval number relative to the E circle.
